<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I understand the full picture. Case number validation follows a specific order: first check for junk patterns like `^[%._\\-/A-Za-z0-9]+$`, then validate year format with `[0-9]{4}`, and finally match the accepted pattern. The golden-fixtures show `%%%NOT-A-CASE-ID%%%` matching junk, `010210001` missing the year format, and valid cases following the accepted pattern. The order matters because a string missing the year format might also match the junk pattern. It has Chinese characters , , etc., so the junk pattern `^[%._\\-/A-Za-z0-9]+$` wouldn't match. For invalid-002 `%%%NOT-A-CASE-ID%%%`, only % and letters match the junk pattern. 

Document extraction requires markers like , , and  for civil judgments. A pipeline mismatch occurs with  lacking  markers. Court name snippet can be the first line, such as "". Case numbers are extracted via regex, cause snippets come from , and judgement dates are parsed from .

For compliance, use regex `\d{15,}` for deterministic matching. Literal_any is used for  and , which are flagged as suspicious. For the suspicious-only fixture, only the keyword "" is present, not a 15+ digit sequence. However, for the deterministic-hit case, the value `9876543210123456789` matches the regex `\d{15,}` due to being a 19-digit number. For clean documents with no long digits or keywords, no findings are extracted. Rule evaluation order ensures that deterministic regex does not trigger on suspicious-only cases lacking 15+ consecutive digits. The library version string uses `stdlib-case-number@v0.1.0-demo`, matching the expected format. The implementation plan adopts a single Spring Boot application with packages under `com.competition.legaldev.stdlib` for the loader. The services are organized under `com.competition.legaldev` with packages for `caseno`, `extract`, `compliance`, and `web`. The `application.yml` configures `app.stdlib.base-path` or classpath resources, sets a 10-second processing timeout, and defines Tomcat threads for around 20 concurrent comments. YAML loading uses Jackson and SnakeYAML, both included via `spring-boot-starter`. Invalid case number messages must be non-empty according to invariants. Expected JSON fixtures don't always include the `message` field; I will use `summary_zh` or a standard message from YAML for consistency. Although OpenAPI doesn't require `message` in `CaseNumberValidateResponse`, invariants state that for `valid=false`, the message must be non-empty, and for `valid=true`, it can be empty. To ensure consistency, I will include the `message` field in all responses. Messages for case numbers should use `summary_zh` fields from YAML when available. For invalid case number 001, the message can be derived from the rule CN-YEAR-SP-404 summary. Valid expected responses may omit the message field, which is acceptable when `valid=true`. For timeouts, HTTP 504 with ErrorResponse will be used for global timeouts, and HTTP 422 with PARSE_TIMEOUT for document parsing timeouts. The README placeholder indicates these statuses should be filled in accordingly.
